logic.note: IN above ~1 V (0.3 mA into the base) switches the transistor on; PWM on IN chops the motor at that duty.

timing.note: Spin-up / spin-down with a 40 ms time constant (typical for 10 mm coin motors: 30–80 ms).

analog.note: 3 V coin ERM as a brushed DC motor (12 000 rpm and 75 mA at 3 V, 120 mA stall) through a saturated NPN (~0.15 V). Vibration strength is reported as speed relative to the rated speed; real vibration force grows with the square of speed.

power.note: Motor current comes from VCC; IN draws under 5 mA from the pin.

emulates: On/off and PWM strength from a GPIO through the module's transistor
doesNotEmulate: The vibration itself (g-force, how it feels through a case)
Start failures at low PWM duty (real coin motors need ~40 % to start)
testOnRealDevice: How strong it feels inside your enclosure
The lowest PWM duty that still starts the motor
